title: Accenture Technology Vision 2013: Every Business Is a Digital Business
notes: Seven trends. Published date from PDF creation date (2013-02-22). The Research Methodology gives no fixed horizon ('in the years ahead'), so no edition-level horizon is recorded. Quotes are the deck line printed under each trend title.

entries.label: Relationships at Scale
entries.quote: Moving beyond transactions to digital relationships
entries.subject: Digital customer relationships
entries.note: Deck line under the title; body: 'companies can manage relationships with consumers at scale.'

entries.label: Design for Analytics
entries.quote: Formulate the questions, and design for the answers
entries.subject: Analytics-driven software design
entries.note: Body: 'The current generation of software was designed for functionality. The next generation must be designed for analytics as well.'

entries.label: Data Velocity
entries.quote: Matching the speed of decision to the speed of action
entries.subject: Real-time data analytics
entries.note: Cites Gartner: in-memory computing adoption expected to increase threefold by 2015 (third-party estimate, not Accenture's).

entries.label: Seamless Collaboration
entries.quote: Right channel, right worker, right job
entries.subject: Enterprise social collaboration

entries.label: Software-Defined Networking
entries.subject: Software-defined networking
entries.note: Cites IDC (Dec 2012): SDN market from $360 million in 2013 to $3.7 billion by 2016 (third-party estimate).

entries.label: Beyond the Cloud
entries.quote: Accenture estimates that by 2016, enterprises will devote 14 percent of their overall IT product and services spending to cloud, up from 5 percent in 2011.
entries.subject: Cloud computing
entries.metric: share of enterprise IT product and services spending devoted to cloud
entries.note: Deck line under the title: 'The value lies in putting the cloud to work'. Quote is Accenture's own estimate from the chapter body.
